passage:
In a 2019 article in Science, Kenneth Rosenberg and colleagues reported a net loss of nearly three billion breeding birds from North America between 1970 and 2017, with grassland species suffering the steepest losses of any biome. The researchers distinguished grassland-obligate species, whose breeding range is essentially confined to native grassland, from grassland-associated species, which breed in grasslands but also use other open habitats. They concluded that the obligate species fared considerably worse than the associated species, because _______

Estimated change in North American breeding population, 1970-2017 (selected species)
| Species | Habitat class | Change (%) |
|---|---|---|
| Eastern Meadowlark | Grassland-obligate | -72 |
| Bobolink | Grassland-obligate | -65 |
| Vesper Sparrow | Grassland-associated | -36 |
| Field Sparrow | Grassland-associated | -30 |
question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.text: Vesper Sparrow declined by 36 percent, the smaller of the two declines among grassland-associated species in the table.
Eastern Meadowlark showed the largest decline in the table, at 72 percent, the steepest single drop among the four species.
Eastern Meadowlark, a grassland-obligate species, declined by 72 percent, while Field Sparrow, a grassland-associated species, declined by only 30 percent.
the two grassland-obligate species declined by 72 and 65 percent, while the two grassland-associated species declined by only 36 and 30 percent.

explanation: The correct answer is D. The claim compares the two habitat classes as groups, so the completion must show that both obligate species declined more steeply than both associated species. D pairs the obligate declines (72 and 65 percent) against the associated declines (36 and 30 percent), supporting the conclusion directly. A and B each cite a single species and never compare the classes; C compares only one species from each class, a weaker basis for a claim about the groups as a whole.
